title: Paladin Security onboarding eval manifest and signoff
overview: This document is the customer-specific onboarding evaluation manifest for Paladin Security (triage assistant). It consolidates pinned prompts, private dataset descriptions, quantitative acceptance criteria, regression test slate, and the sign-off process required to certify a model variant for production serving under the Paladin Dedicated instance. This is intended to be a working artifact: expect updates during the canary run and A/B review.
pinned_prompts: Triage summary: Given the alert details, output a concise 2-3 sentence remediation summary, list probable root causes with confidence scores (0-1), and recommend immediate next steps prioritized by impact.
Escalation decision: For a supplied alert and historical context, decide whether to auto-close, require analyst review, or escalate to SOC Tier 2. Include the key evidence that drove the decision.
False positive probe: Given an alert and two preceding events, determine whether the alert is likely benign. Explain reasoning and which feature(s) most influenced the judgement.
User-friendly explanation: Convert a technical triage decision into a short message (one paragraph) suitable for a non-technical customer-facing ticket update.
Indicator normalization: Extract and canonicalize network indicators from free-text logs into fields (ip, domain, filename, hash) and tag confidence for each extraction.
private_datasets: PS_ALERTS_V1 — 12,450 labeled triage records (alert text, analyst verdict, remediation) — redacted PII, retained in encrypted bucket (s3://redwood-private/paladin/ps_alerts_v1)
PS_INCIDENT_HISTORY_2019_2023 — 3,200 incident timelines with linked alerts and post-incident root cause analyses — used for escalation decision baseline
PS_FP_ADVERSARIAL_SET_2024 — 1,000 synthetic adversarial cases crafted by Paladin SOC to validate false-positive resilience
PS_METADATA_FEATURES — feature dump (metadata vectors) used for similarity checks and embedding evaluation (hashed ids only)
acceptance_criteria: Precision@1 for 'recommended remediation' >= 0.82 measured on a held-out labeled set (PS_ALERTS_V1 holdout)
Escalation decision accuracy >= 0.88 (macro-averaged over three classes: auto-close, review, escalate)
P95 end-to-end latency (inference + routing overhead) <= 150ms in Dedicated canary util under production routing mix
Embedding similarity stability: average cosine drift <= 0.03 between candidate model and baseline for canonical indicators
No semantic regressions on the top-100 pinned prompts (human-rated quality delta <= 0.05 on 0-1 scale)
Model quantization/ort variant must not increase hallucination incidents on PS_INCIDENT_HISTORY by more than 5% relative to baseline
regression_tests_and_procedures: Pinned prompt sweep: run all pinned_prompts with PS_ALERTS_V1 holdout and collect top-1 outputs for human rating (3 raters, blind) — pass if mean rating >= 0.75
Adversarial injection: run PS_FP_ADVERSARIAL_SET_2024 and measure FP rate — automated assert triggers Slack alert if >0.15
Temporal drift check: sample last 90 days of alerts (anonymized) and compare model outputs to baseline; flag if escalation accuracy drops by >0.04
Metric regression bundling: collect token-level cost, median latency, and per-route error rates; if any metric regresses beyond configured thresholds, block rollout
Manual spot checks: Solutions engineering to audit 25 random canary outputs across different customer tenants for label alignment
Eval harness reproducibility: store random seeds, model sha, and eval script hash with each run (artifact linked in linked_artifacts)
signoff_steps: Pre-canary: engineering and applied-ml approve dataset freshness and eval harness (Asha + Dmitri)
Canary: deploy model variant to Paladin Dedicated pool at 5% traffic for 72 hours — monitor automated gates (latency, errors, quality)
Canary review: compile canary report; stakeholders (Paladin SOC lead, Jordan Blake, Lina Morales) to review within 3 business days
A/B (if requested): run 50/50 comparison for 7 days and confirm no customer-visible regressions
Final signoff: product and customer success sign (Jordan Blake, Paladin CSM) and eng-applied-ml sign (Asha Patel) — record signatures in Confluence and attach final eval artifacts
Rollback plan: immediate traffic revert to previous model, run quick repro eval, and open PS-rollback Jira ticket if quality or stability failures observed
operational_notes: Observability hooks must include per-prompt latency, token cost, and agreement rate vs. baseline. Add an exception policy for high-cost long-hallucination prompts so requests are rate-limited. For private datasets, access is limited to eng-applied-ml and Paladin contacts; datasets are versioned and immutable for any signed-off model variant.

notes: This file is intentionally granular because Paladin requires traceability for each acceptance criterion and an auditable trail for any private dataset use. Keep edits minimal after signoff; append new versions as separate manifests (e.g., v2) rather than in-place edits.
